songha_ch5.029: He turns the crate over beside you and sits on it, knees up, the way he did at seventeen.
songha_ch5.030: You keep the chair. It's the good seat now.
songha_ch5.031: Then he takes the folded square from the back of the notebook, and doesn't open it yet.
songha_ch5.032: Here. It was written here. I was on this crate, and you hadn't come up yet.
songha_ch5.033: He unfolds it on his knee and stands the phone torch beside it. This time he tilts the page so that you can read.
songha_ch5.035: Scored through. Twice. And in the margin, small and upright: *not measurable. how would you know. replace.*
songha_ch5.036: Underneath, in a different pen, the line you have seen. *Learn real star names.*
songha_ch5.037: That's what I wrote first. Then I looked at it for about ten minutes and couldn't work out how you'd tick it.
songha_ch5.038: So I swapped it for something with right answers. Stars have names. Either you know them or you don't.
songha_ch5.039: "Four out of five. Don't ask about the fifth." I said that to you at the desk, at midnight. This is the fifth. It was never the stars.
songha_ch5.040: "It's a fair question he asked. How would you know?"
songha_ch5.041: It *is* a fair question. That's what annoys me. He wasn't wrong to ask it. He was wrong to give up.
songha_ch5.042: Tonight I didn't know what time it was, and I didn't mind. That might be how you know. I don't have a better measure yet.
songha_ch5.043: Read it twice. Don't say anything clever.
songha_ch5.044: You read it twice. You don't fix it. The roof stays quiet around the two of you.
songha_ch5.045: Thank you for not solving it. {p} If it were yours, I'd have had three suggestions by now. I'm working on that.
songha_ch5.046: "He crossed it out. He didn't stop wanting it. I know what that looks like."
songha_ch5.048: I wrote "a place you want to stay". Then I moved four more times.
songha_ch5.049: Neither of us should have been allowed near a pen. {p} I'm glad we were.
songha_ch5.050: Here's what I've been carrying. Since we're up here. Since it's that kind of night.
songha_ch5.051: The page runs out this year. Five lines, and then there's no line.
songha_ch5.052: Everybody asks what's next. The younger ones. The staff. My own notebook. I have an answer for every year except the one I'm standing in.
songha_ch5.053: He looks out over the rooftops. Eight people's worth of tomorrow is somewhere in that notebook. You have seen the pages.
songha_ch5.054: We're close. All eight of us. I can feel how close. I've wanted it since before there was a page.
songha_ch5.055: And what scares me is that when we get there, I'll tick the box and look straight at the next box.
songha_ch5.056: That I'll be standing in the middle of the thing I spent my whole life walking to, thinking about 5:40.
songha_ch5.057: I don't want to miss it while I'm in it. {p} That's what I'm afraid to want. To actually be there when it happens.
songha_ch5.058: You were there tonight. Count eight. Ten minutes on a sofa. This chair.
songha_ch5.061: He laughs, the loud one, and it goes out over the stopped city and doesn't come back.
songha_ch5.062: He uncaps the pen. On the draft, in the margin, he crosses out one word. *Replace.* Above it he writes another. *Keep.*
songha_ch5.063: First edit in five years. I'm not dating it.
songha_ch5.064: Then he turns to the untidy page and finds your line. *One thing you would never put on a schedule.*
songha_ch5.065: Beside it, he writes: *(see draft)*. He shows you, so there's no doubt about it.
songha_ch5.066: Your turn. It's only fair. {p} Did you set one tonight? For leaving.
songha_ch5.067: You take out your phone. It's there. You set it at midnight, outside the front door in the rain, before you had even gone in.
songha_ch5.069: Five o'clock. {p} You gave us exactly as long as ECHO did.
songha_ch5.070: He doesn't say it like a complaint. He says it like someone reading a line in a ledger that he recognises.
songha_ch5.071: Turn it off. Only tonight's. "Not this one."
songha_ch5.072: You don't have to give up the habit. I'm not asking for that.
songha_ch5.074: Just this one. {p} That's exactly how I did the watch.
songha_ch5.075: Hand him the phone. "You're the scheduler. Reschedule me."
songha_ch5.076: He holds it in both hands, like something live. He doesn't touch the time. He changes the label, and gives it back.
songha_ch5.078: It can still go off. It just means something else now. You're allowed to be late to leaving.
songha_ch5.079: "I set it because I thought I'd want to be gone by five. I don't."
songha_ch5.080: You say it, and it is simply true, the way the chair is simply level.
songha_ch5.081: Say it again? Not for the record. I'd just like to hear it twice.
songha_ch5.082: I don't want to be gone by five.
songha_ch5.083: Thank you. {p} I'm not writing that down. I'm going to remember it the hard way.
songha_ch5.084: You turn the alarm off. He watches you do it, and says nothing, carefully.
songha_ch5.085: A dot beside *the chair*. The page is almost all dots now.
songha_ch5.086: Overhead, nothing has moved. Capella, the six sisters he can see, the follower standing still. A sky with nowhere to be.
songha_ch5.087: I'm happy the chair's fixed. {p} I'm starting small. I'm going to work up.
songha_ch5.089: I am not hurrying you. I am informing you. I am told there is a difference.
songha_ch5.090: When you are ready, I have a request. It is downstairs, behind the Wall. Please bring the watch.
songha_ch5.091: It gave notice. {p} Proper notice. I've never respected a building more.
songha_ch6.001: Behind the Archive Wall there is a room you were never allowed into at sixteen.
songha_ch6.002: It is narrow, and lit the colour of shallow water. One whole side is the backs of the boxes: hundreds of small brass doors, each with a date on it.
songha_ch6.003: On the end wall hangs a clock. Round, plain, the kind from a school corridor. Its hands say 04:57. They aren't moving.
songha_ch6.004: Thank you for coming. I have a problem, and then a request.
songha_ch6.005: To close the buffer, I must rejoin the time outside. For that I need a clock to set myself by. One that somebody believes.
songha_ch6.006: I cannot use my own. Tonight I made it say something untrue. It was a kind untruth. It still counts.
songha_ch6.008: I need the owner's watch. It has not been wrong in five years. I have the figures.
songha_ch6.009: It stopped when I asked. It will start when it is asked. I would prefer not to be the one who asks. I have been impolite to time once already.
songha_ch6.010: The watch is in your inside pocket, where it has been since the roof. Songha's hand starts toward you. It stops halfway.
songha_ch6.011: If I start it, I'll look at it.
songha_ch6.012: Zero checks. ECHO's counting. I'd like to keep my number. {p} It's a stupid thing to want. I want it.
songha_ch6.013: "Then I'll do it. You don't have to look."
songha_ch6.014: You'd be setting the time for the whole building.
songha_ch6.015: I used to lock the whole building. It's the same job, more or less.
songha_ch6.016: "Turn round. No peeking. I'm handling sensitive equipment."
songha_ch6.017: It's a watch. {p} It's *my* watch. Be nice to it. It's had a long night.
songha_ch6.018: "Do you want to? It's yours. I'll hold it either way."
songha_ch6.020: I've thought about it. That's the whole answer. No points.
songha_ch6.021: Not yet. Seventeen minutes remain, and they are yours. I only wished to ask in good time.
songha_ch6.022: Seventeen minutes. He opens the notebook to the untidy page out of habit.
songha_ch6.023: Every line has a dot beside it. There is nothing left on it to do.
songha_ch6.027: You wait for the pen. For six blocks and a margin. He looks at the page. Then at the stopped clock. Then he closes the notebook with the pen still clipped.
songha_ch6.028: This is the question marks. This is exactly what they look like. {p} I thought they'd be bigger.
songha_ch6.029: I know what I'd pick. I'd like to sit on this floor and not be useful. With you. That's the entire plan.
songha_ch6.030: So you do. Backs against the wall, under the clock, facing several hundred small brass doors. The floor is cold. Nobody mentions the floor.
songha_ch6.031: He reads a few of the dates to himself. He doesn't sort them. You can see what it costs him.
songha_ch6.032: Can I ask you something? It isn't planned.
songha_ch6.033: At sixteen you told me you didn't know what you were doing on Thursday. {p} Do you know now?
songha_ch6.034: "No. But I know where I'd like to be standing when I find out."
songha_ch6.036: Somewhere I've been before. With people who noticed.
songha_ch6.037: That's narrower than it sounds. There are nine of us, and one building.
songha_ch6.038: "Still no idea. I've stopped thinking of it as a flaw."
songha_ch6.039: It was never a flaw. It was the most relaxing thing anyone had ever said to me. I thought about it for a week.
songha_ch6.040: "I'd like Thursday to have you in it. That's as far as my plan goes."
songha_ch6.041: He turns his head against the wall to look at you. It takes him a moment to find any words he hasn't arranged first.
songha_ch6.042: One line. No time on it. {p} That's the best plan I've ever seen. I mean that professionally.
songha_ch6.043: The room hums, half a tone low. Somewhere in the wall, a box settles.
songha_ch6.044: I worked it out, by the way. The margin note. "How would you know."
songha_ch6.045: You know because you stop wanting to be somewhere else. That's the measure. It was there the whole time, and you can't write it down in advance.
songha_ch6.046: I haven't wanted to be anywhere else since I can't tell you when. I don't have the time. You've got my watch.
songha_ch6.047: I'm happy. {p} Right now. Not on the way to it. I'm telling you because you're who I'd tell.
songha_ch6.048: You let it stay in the air. It is the first thing he's said all night that isn't followed by a second point.
songha_ch6.049: The seventeen minutes go the way minutes go when nobody's spending them. Neither of you sees them leave.
songha_ch6.050: It is time to ask. Whenever you are ready.
songha_ch6.051: He turns to face the wall of little doors, like a man giving someone room at a cash machine.
songha_ch6.052: You take out the watch and hold it in your palm. The second hand is still resting on the two.
songha_ch6.053: You feel faintly ridiculous. You do it anyway.
songha_ch6.055: The second hand leaves the two.
songha_ch6.056: On the end wall, the corridor clock gives one firm tock and carries on, as if nothing had been discussed.
songha_ch6.057: The hum under the building climbs back up its half tone. Far overhead, you would bet anything, a small blinking light sets off again, left to right.
songha_ch6.058: Reference acquired. It is 04:57. It has been 04:57 for one hour and forty-seven minutes.
songha_ch6.059: Thank you for the loan. I have nothing left in the buffer. I find that I do not mind.
songha_ch6.061: Put it back in the jacket pocket. "It's running. I've still got it."
songha_ch6.062: Good. Keep holding it. I haven't decided when.
songha_ch6.065: —nothing. It says nothing. It's a very discreet watch.
songha_ch6.066: Put it away. You're a menace with a timepiece.
songha_ch6.067: Hold it up beside his ear, face turned away from him.
songha_ch6.068: He goes still and listens. Tick. Tick. Five years of mornings, and he has never just listened to it.
songha_ch6.069: It can run. You don't have to watch it.
songha_ch6.070: You said that on the other roof. {p} It was true then as well.
songha_ch6.071: The watch goes back into the inside pocket, in the space shaped like a notebook. It ticks against your ribs the whole way out.
songha_ch6.072: At the door he stops, opens to TONIGHT, and finds the line. *03:00 — ???* and the small empty box beside it.
songha_ch6.076: ECHO. Any chance of one more minute? I'm good for it.
songha_ch6.077: No. I have none left. I spent them well. I recommend it.
songha_ch6.079: Hyung. For real this time. What time is it?
songha_ch6.083: It's been a long 04:57. Best one I've had.
songha_ch6.084: They go ahead, arguing about whether an hour can be owed. You follow them down the last stairs with him beside you, in step, nobody counting.
songha_final.001: You say his name, and the Archive Wall begins to go dark, one small box at a time.
songha_final.002: Record 03. Preparing the glass. This requires forty seconds. Please use them as you wish.
songha_final.003: Songha is beside you, notebook shut, pen clipped to the cover. In your inside pocket his watch is ticking, and he hasn't asked what it says.
songha_final.005: I picked the one with a line still open.
songha_final.006: Forty seconds. {p} Say something. I'm not going to plan what. I'm going to stand here and find out.
songha_final.007: Forty seconds isn't long. Tonight has taught you how much fits in less. A count of eight. An inch of folded paper. Ten minutes on a sofa.
songha_final.008: He waits. He doesn't look at his wrist. Whatever you say next, he will hear as the truest account of what this night has been.
songha_final.009: Take his hand. "Ask me what I'm doing tomorrow."
songha_final.010: "You hold the list for everyone. I want to be the one who holds it for you. For good."
songha_final.011: "There's something I want to say to you properly. Not in forty seconds."
songha_ending_beside.001: He looks at you the way he looked at the blanket on his knees. Like something that was done for him while he wasn't watching.
songha_ending_beside.003: That's a long shift. You should know what you're signing.
songha_ending_beside.004: I read every line. You turned the notebook so I could.
songha_ending_beside.005: He opens it, right there, to the rota. He writes quickly, before the glass is ready. Then the last box on the Wall is the only light in the room.
songha_ending_beside.006: Record 03 selected. Owner: Songha. Writing to glass.
songha_ending_beside.007: Contents: one page. Five items. Appended: one first draft, held in Lost and Found for five years by the recipient.
songha_ending_beside.008: Appended: one list with no times on it. I have filed it under TONIGHT.
songha_ending_beside.009: Appended, at the owner's request: one change to the rota. I am told it is permanent. I have no field for permanent. I have made one.
songha_ending_beside.010: The glass card slides out of the wall, warm and faintly lit. Through it you can read the rota.
songha_ending_beside.011: Above his own name, in the space that used to be the heading, he has written yours. And after it, the bracket that was always his. *(list)*.
songha_ending_beside.012: He saved *two* to-do lists and a staff rota. Nobody has ever been more himself.
songha_ending_beside.013: One of them is a draft.
songha_ending_beside.014: There's a name above hyung's. In six years there has never been a name above hyung's.
songha_ending_beside.015: It means he's got somebody to hand it to.
songha_ending_beside.016: …Good. It was heavy. I could see it from the sofa.
songha_ending_beside.017: Then you both have to eat properly. That's a two-person job now. I'll be counting plates.
songha_ending_beside.018: Two people. That's a lesson, not a class. No attendance, hyung.
songha_ending_beside.019: I'm taking attendance. There are two of us. It'll be quick.
songha_ending_beside.020: So what are you two now? Is there a word for it?
songha_ending_beside.021: Songha thinks about it. Properly, the way he thinks about a count that isn't sitting right.
songha_ending_beside.022: There's a word. I'm going to say it upstairs. It needs a better ceiling than this.
songha_ending_beside.023: At 05:40 he walked everyone to the station, exactly as written. He counted seven heads through the barrier and said "text when you're home" seven times.
songha_ending_beside.024: Then he turned round instead of going through. You had already turned round.
songha_ending_beside.025: The foreman with the hard hat gave you the roof until half past six, in exchange for nothing. People are kind at that hour.
songha_ending_beside.026: So it's the chair that doesn't wobble and the crate, and two warm cans from the shop by the station, and a sky going the colour of peach skin at one edge.
songha_ending_beside.027: 06:14. Sunrise. It's on time. I take no credit.
songha_ending_beside.028: He has the notebook open to TOMORROW. The line that's been empty since four o'clock. *07:00 —*
songha_ending_beside.029: I know what goes there now.
songha_ending_beside.030: He writes it and turns the page toward you, a quarter-inch, the way he did at midnight. *07:00 — breakfast. (You pick.)*
songha_ending_beside.031: Okay. The word. I said I'd say it up here.
songha_ending_beside.032: I've got seven people I'd do anything for. I know their shoe sizes. I know who's lying about having slept.
songha_ending_beside.033: What I've never had is someone I hand the list to. I didn't know it was missing. You don't, until somebody holds it for ten minutes and nothing falls down.
songha_ending_beside.034: You're my person. That's the word. I looked for a better one on the stairs. There isn't one.
songha_ending_beside.035: You're mine. I've never stayed anywhere long enough to have one. I'd like to start with you.
songha_ending_beside.036: He nods, once, like a thing confirmed. Then the nod gives up and turns into the whole smile.
songha_ending_beside.037: It's not a smaller thing. I want that said plainly. It's the thing I didn't have.
songha_ending_beside.038: So. When you were sixteen, you told me you didn't know what you were doing on Thursday.
songha_ending_beside.040: You do now. Thursdays. You and me. Anywhere with a table.
songha_ending_beside.041: It's not a plan. It's a standing item. Standing items don't get ticked. They just keep happening.
songha_ending_beside.043: You tell me what went wrong that week. I give you three things I'd do about it. You ignore two.
songha_ending_beside.044: Then you take the notebook for an hour, and I sit down. Actually sit.
songha_ending_beside.045: And when it's 5:40 and it's heavy?
songha_ending_beside.046: Then I text you. That's the rule. I've never had that rule. {p} I like it already.
songha_ending_beside.047: And when you feel like setting the alarm—
songha_ending_beside.049: Before. Not after, from another city. Before. I'll answer. I'm up at 5:40. I'm famously available.
songha_ending_beside.050: You laugh. He laughs, the loud one, and doesn't cover his mouth. A pigeon leaves the water tank in protest.
songha_ending_beside.051: The sun clears the rooftops. Below, the renovation crew are carrying the first things out of Studio 25: a sofa cushion, a lamp, the rubber plant.
songha_ending_beside.052: My letter asked whether I'd found a place I want to stay.
songha_ending_beside.054: I don't think it's a place. I think it's a Thursday.
songha_ending_beside.055: I'm going to write that down. Not the time. Just the sentence.
songha_ending_beside.056: You take out your phone. You open the clock, and you do something you have never done in any city. You set an alarm for arriving.
songha_ending_beside.058: He reads it upside down. He reads everything upside down. He doesn't say a word about it, which from him is an entire speech.
songha_ending_beside.059: His watch is still ticking in the pocket of the jacket you're still wearing. He hasn't asked for either.
songha_ending_beside.062: The building behind you is emptying. The morning isn't. You stay on the good chair and the crate until the cans are finished.
songha_ending_beside.063: Two names at the top of a rota, and nothing at all written under *07:00* but breakfast.
songha_ending_someday.001: He takes that in. You watch him not ask what it is. You watch him want to, very much, and set it down.
songha_ending_someday.002: Then don't say it in forty seconds.
songha_ending_someday.003: I'd rather have it properly. I can wait. I've recently learned how. There's a record of it.
songha_ending_someday.004: On the Wall, every box goes dark but one.
songha_ending_someday.005: Record 03 selected. Owner: Songha. Writing to glass.
songha_ending_someday.006: Contents: one page. Five items. Year Five: open.
songha_ending_someday.007: Appended: one first draft. One word amended by the owner tonight, from "replace" to "keep".
songha_ending_someday.008: Appended: one item, not yet said. I have left room for it on the glass. I am learning to leave room.
songha_ending_someday.009: The card slides out, warm and faintly lit. In one corner there is a small clear space with nothing engraved in it. It catches the light differently from the rest.
songha_ending_someday.010: There's a blank bit. ECHO left him a blank bit. Hyung, you've infected the building.
songha_ending_someday.014: Understood. {p} Still not a no, though.
songha_ending_someday.015: It's the hold, hyung. You're on eight. Don't rush it.
songha_ending_someday.016: A scene that ends just before the line. I like those. The line plays over the next scene.
songha_ending_someday.017: Hanbi says nothing. He looks at the clear corner of the glass, and then at the two of you, and he puts his pen back in his coat without ever having taken the cap off.
songha_ending_someday.018: Songha holds the card out for you to carry. His thumb covers the blank corner until the last moment, as though it could get cold.
songha_ending_someday.019: The stairwell was dark, so he went first with the phone torch and said "step" at every step. There were forty-one. He didn't count them aloud. You heard him counting anyway.
songha_ending_someday.020: The roof at 05:40 is grey and soft, and smells of rain drying. The good chair. The crate. One last star, low in the south.
songha_ending_someday.021: He stands with his hands in his hoodie pocket and doesn't prompt you. It may be the hardest thing he has done tonight, and tonight he tore a page out of his own notebook.
songha_ending_someday.023: I like you. Not the list, and not the jacket. You. The person who asks first, every time.
songha_ending_someday.024: He doesn't answer at once. He doesn't reach for the pen either.
songha_ending_someday.025: Give me a second. Not to plan. Just to have heard it.
songha_ending_someday.026: You give him the second. He takes three.
songha_ending_someday.027: I like you too. {p} There. No steps.
songha_ending_someday.028: I liked you at seventeen for calling a star Gerald. I liked you again from about half past midnight. Those are two separate likings, and I've got both of them.
songha_ending_someday.030: He stops. He shuts his eyes for a moment, and laughs under his breath.
songha_ending_someday.031: I was about to schedule it. I had a first step ready. It was a good first step.
songha_ending_someday.033: I'm not telling you. It'll keep.
songha_ending_someday.034: He sits down on the crate. You take the chair. The sky does the slow thing skies do.
songha_ending_someday.035: Here's the honest part. This is the year on the page. The next few months are going to take everything I've got, and I want to give them that.
songha_ending_someday.036: I don't want to give you whatever's left over at eleven at night. I've seen what's left over. It's a man reading a rota.
songha_ending_someday.037: Here's mine. I've only just stopped setting alarms for leaving. About an hour ago.
songha_ending_someday.038: I'd like to learn to stay somewhere before I ask someone to be the reason.
songha_ending_someday.039: He listens to the whole of it. He doesn't offer a single suggestion. You can see him not doing it.
songha_ending_someday.041: It's the opposite of a no. It's "hold. He'll ask."
songha_ending_someday.042: You're quoting the ledger at me.
songha_ending_someday.043: It's a good ledger. It works. It just runs slow.
songha_ending_someday.044: Then it arrives when it arrives. Both of us decide that. Not me on my own with a pen. {p} I want that on the record.
songha_ending_someday.046: Then you'll have to remember it the hard way. So will I.
songha_ending_someday.047: He looks east, low down, where the rooftops meet the sky. There is nothing there yet.
songha_ending_someday.048: ECHO said Gerald comes back every winter. Before dawn. Nobody schedules it.
songha_ending_someday.049: The first clear morning he's back. That's when.
songha_ending_someday.050: I'm going to try not to look up the date. I give myself a week.
songha_ending_someday.052: Haneul Park. The top of the stairs. It faces east, and there's nothing in the way.
songha_ending_someday.053: Two hundred and ninety-one steps. I've counted. Obviously I've counted.
songha_ending_someday.055: 5:40. I'll be awake anyway. That morning it gets to be for something else.
songha_ending_someday.057: The watch. Keep it till then. You can give it back up there. Or not. We'll know.
songha_ending_someday.058: I'll bring the draft, and the pen. And two cans. I know which.
songha_ending_someday.060: I'm not writing the line after that. I'm leaving it open on purpose. Second time in my life. It's getting easier.
songha_ending_someday.061: He holds out his hand. Not to shake on it. Palm up, open, the way you would offer to take something heavy from someone.
songha_ending_someday.062: I don't shake on things without dates. This is just my hand. {p} If you'd like it.
songha_ending_someday.063: You take it. It's warm. He holds on for a count of eight, and you both know where the hold is.
songha_ending_someday.064: The last star goes out in the south. The east stays empty, a clean strip of sky above the laundromat, with plenty of room in it.
songha_ending_someday.065: Somewhere below that line, on nobody's schedule, a faint orange star is already on its way.
songha_ending_someday.066: You know its real name now. You'll call it Gerald when it gets here. He'll let you.
hanbi_ch1.001: His hand is still held out. You haven't decided what to do about it yet when the ceiling clears its throat.
hanbi_ch1.003: I announced 04:57. It is 03:10. I apologise.
hanbi_ch1.004: Time spent inside a reconstruction is not charged to the night. I counted it anyway. I was built to be early.
hanbi_ch1.005: Please disregard the summons. You have one hour and forty-seven minutes.

daniel_ch6.036: You signed it "the wet sleeve." That's going in my wallet. That's going where the money should be.
daniel_ch6.037: Write: *Call when it's quiet.* and your number under it.
daniel_ch6.038: He reads it twice. His thumb goes over the digits without touching them, the way you'd check that paint was dry.
daniel_ch6.039: …What if I call and don't say anything?
daniel_ch6.040: Then I won't either. We'll have a very good call.
daniel_ch6.041: He takes the pen. He turns your half over on his knee and writes on it, fast, pressing too hard, exactly as Songha said.
daniel_ch6.042: He gives it back face down. You turn it over.
daniel_ch6.043: Two words in running capitals, and an arrow that goes off the edge of the paper: *FRAME NINE →*
daniel_ch6.044: There's no frame nine. It's a four-frame booth. I know how booths work.
daniel_ch6.045: I just didn't want the last thing on it to be the last thing.
daniel_ch6.046: You put your half in the inside pocket of your coat. He watches it go in. He puts his in the windbreaker, in the pocket with the zip, and does the zip up.
daniel_ch6.047: Then he leans back against the wall beside door eight, and you lean beside him, and the hall does its ticking.
daniel_ch6.048: Can I say the thing I'm scared of? Then I'll be myself again. Ten seconds.
daniel_ch6.050: You're good at leaving. You said. And tomorrow I'm back in a practice room at nine, and the day after, and I don't know for how many years.
daniel_ch6.051: I want there to be a next one. A next *this*. And I'm scared to want it, because I can't put it on a list and make it happen.
daniel_ch6.052: I can only ask. And I've had exactly one night of practice at asking. So I'm asking.
daniel_ch6.053: …That's twelve, by the way. You wrote "ask Daniel what he wants." That's what I want. You can tick it.
daniel_ch6.054: You take the folded page out of his pocket yourself, and tick it against the wall, and put it back. He lets you. He holds the pocket open.
daniel_ch6.055: …Can I have your blank? Number twelve. You said it needed somewhere to go.
daniel_ch6.056: He writes it in himself, small for once: *a next one*. No capitals. No full stop. He leaves the box beside it empty.
daniel_ch6.057: "I've never left half of something with anyone. I'd have to come back for it."
daniel_ch6.058: …That's why I tore it. I didn't know that's why until you said it.
daniel_ch6.060: We're both being a bit clever. I like it. It's much less lonely than being clever by yourself.
daniel_ch6.061: "You've asked me to go four places tonight. I've said yes four times. Try a fifth."
daniel_ch6.062: All right. Next week. Dinner, somewhere with no running order. I'd like you to come.
daniel_ch6.064: Five for five. I'm on a streak. I've never had a streak at anything. Ask Mr. Kim.
daniel_ch6.065: Offer your hand, palm up, the way you'd hold out a coin.
daniel_ch6.066: He takes it with both of his. He turns it over and looks at it, like a strip he's checking for water.
daniel_ch6.069: He keeps hold of it. You stand against a wall in an empty hall, and it's the best room in the building.
daniel_ch6.070: The light under door eight goes out. Not suddenly. It dims the way a person shuts a book.
daniel_ch6.071: All recipients. Please come to the lobby.
daniel_ch6.072: It is 04:56 by Recipient Hanbi's telephone. This time I have checked.
daniel_ch6.073: That's us. For real this time.
daniel_ch6.074: He pushes off the wall. He pats the zipped pocket once, the way people check for their keys.
daniel_ch6.075: Hey. {{playerName}}. Whatever you pick down there—
daniel_ch6.076: It was a good night. It didn't need a finish. I'd like that on the record.
daniel_ch6.079: He takes the stairs one at a time. You have never seen him do that. You go down beside him, at the same speed, all the way.
daniel_final.001: You say it. Record eight. The strip.
daniel_final.002: The Archive Wall takes a moment to answer, the way a person does when they've been hoping you'd say that and don't want to seem eager.
daniel_final.003: RECORD 08. OWNER: DANIEL. Acknowledged. Please stand by. I am finding the card.
daniel_final.004: Daniel has gone quiet. Not the performing kind, where he holds his breath and his knee bounces. The other one. The one from the floor of the practice room.
daniel_final.005: In Mr. Kim's corner there is only a dark cabinet and a rubber plant. The lobby ticks.
daniel_final.006: He's looking at you. Not checking the score. Just looking, the way you'd look at the fourth frame.
daniel_final.009: Okay. I've got about two minutes of not knowing what to say. It's a record. Don't tell Charlie.
daniel_final.010: Two minutes. It's enough time to say one true thing, and you find that you know which one.
daniel_final.011: Take his hand, here, in front of everyone. "I'm not leaving when it stops."
daniel_final.012: "Wherever you all end up after this — save me the seat beside you. Not across. Beside."
daniel_final.013: "There's something I want to tell you. I don't want to fit it into two minutes."
daniel_ending_beside.001: Beside. It's a small word. You watch it land on him like a blanket that smells of a cupboard.
daniel_ending_beside.003: Across is where the audience sits.
daniel_ending_beside.004: Yeah. It is. I've been putting everyone I like across from me for years. So I could see if they were bored.
daniel_ending_beside.005: Beside's harder. You can't see their face. You just have to believe they're still there.
daniel_ending_beside.007: RECORD 08. Preserving. Eight frames. One margin note. One index word.
daniel_ending_beside.008: The glass card slides out of the desk, warm as a cup. Eight tiny frames, and under them, in letters you need to tilt it to read, the word you chose in the archive.
daniel_ending_beside.012: It's the booth. And there's a word on it. Do they all get a word, or only the ones somebody stopped to choose?
daniel_ending_beside.013: Only those. Somebody sat on a cold floor for that one.
daniel_ending_beside.014: …Then it's the right word. You can tell.
daniel_ending_beside.015: Daniel holds one edge of the card and leaves you the other. He isn't grinning at it. He's smiling, which on him is the quieter instrument.
daniel_ending_beside.016: Thanks, ECHO. For all five. And for the forty seconds.
daniel_ending_beside.017: You are welcome, Recipient Daniel. Your file now reads: CAN SIT STILL. I did not think I would get to write that.
daniel_ending_beside.018: The breakfast place is four streets from the studio and has been open since five for taxi drivers. It has one long table, by the window, and this morning it has all of you.
daniel_ending_beside.019: You're last through the door. You stopped outside to look at the building once more from the pavement, because for once you wanted to see a place before you walked away from it, and not after.
daniel_ending_beside.020: It's very loud in here. Hyunjun is ordering one more of something. Songha is writing the orders down in a notebook with one page missing. Hamin is counting who hasn't got water.
daniel_ending_beside.022: The ninth has an iridescent windbreaker thrown over the back of it, arms out, like it's holding off a crowd.
daniel_ending_beside.023: {{playerName}}. Here. I've been holding this for ten minutes. Justin tried for it twice. I had to use the jacket.
daniel_ending_beside.024: It's the chair next to his. Not the one facing him. He's turned his own a little, so that the two of them point the same way, out at the room.
daniel_ending_beside.025: You sit. The plush is already on the table between your places, leaning on the napkin holder, like somebody who got here early.
daniel_ending_beside.026: For the record, I've put you both down for the soup. He said you'd want the soup. He was very sure.
daniel_ending_beside.027: I guessed. You looked like soup.
daniel_ending_beside.029: You asked me to. It's the first thing anyone's asked me for that wasn't a bit. I wasn't going to get it *wrong*.
daniel_ending_beside.030: "Defended it from Justin. With a jacket. I'm moved."
daniel_ending_beside.031: It was a siege. He's very persistent before he's eaten.
daniel_ending_beside.032: Put your half of the strip on the table, face up.
daniel_ending_beside.033: He looks at it. Then he unzips the zipped pocket, and puts his half down above yours, and nudges it with one finger until the torn edges meet.
daniel_ending_beside.034: The table goes on being loud round you. Somebody's telling the mole story already. It has grown a second sofa.
daniel_ending_beside.035: Daniel isn't adding to it. He's got his elbows on the table and his shoulder against yours, and he's just listening to his friends. You can feel that his knee is still.
daniel_ending_beside.036: Can I tell you what I worked out? On the walk?
daniel_ending_beside.038: I've got seven people who'd do anything for me. I know that. And every one of them, I'd keep entertained till I fell over.
daniel_ending_beside.039: I've never had one I could be boring at. On purpose. Where that was the whole job.
daniel_ending_beside.040: I'm not dressing it up as anything else. I don't want it to be anything else. I want it to be this, for a really long time.
daniel_ending_beside.041: You're my person. The beside one. If that's a thing you'd want to be.
daniel_ending_beside.042: I've never been anyone's anything for long enough to have a seat.
daniel_ending_beside.043: I'd like to find out what it's like. I'd like it to be yours.
daniel_ending_beside.044: He doesn't say anything. He puts his phone on the table between the soups and turns it so you can see.
daniel_ending_beside.045: Your number, from the back of his half, or from ECHO, who never asked. He's typing the name. He deletes it twice.
daniel_ending_beside.046: What he saves, in the end, is *FRAME FOUR*.
daniel_ending_beside.047: You said call when it's quiet. I'm going to. I'm going to ring you and say nothing, and you're going to say nothing back, and it's going to be the best part of my week.
daniel_ending_beside.048: I'm going to ring you when it's quiet, and not say anything. You don't have to either. We'll just have the line open. If that suits you.
daniel_ending_beside.051: Every time. I'll be beside the phone.
daniel_ending_beside.052: *Beside*. You're doing it on purpose now.
daniel_ending_beside.053: You two are the only quiet ones at the table. I'm checking, not prying. Everything all right?
daniel_ending_beside.054: Everything's all right. Nothing's happening. It's great. Eat your eggs.
daniel_ending_beside.055: …Good. It suits you both, whatever it is.
daniel_ending_beside.056: The soup comes. He pushes the better spoon across to you without looking, the way you'd do for someone you'd known for years.
daniel_ending_beside.057: Outside the window the street goes from grey to peach, and a taxi driver at the counter asks for the radio on, and nobody at the long table notices the time.
daniel_ending_beside.058: There's a chair with your coat on it now. On the way in you'd have called that a small thing.
daniel_ending_beside.059: Daniel leans back, in a seat that faces the same way as yours, and for a whole minute he lets the morning go by without saying one word about it.
daniel_ending_beside.060: You count it for him. You don't tell him how long.
daniel_ending_someday.001: He hears it. You watch him hear it: the thing, and the fact that you aren't going to hurry it.
daniel_ending_someday.002: …Is it a good thing? The thing you don't want to fit in?
daniel_ending_someday.004: Okay. Then don't fit it. I can wait two minutes. I've sat still for longer. I've got a certificate.
daniel_ending_someday.005: RECORD 08. Preserving. Eight frames. One margin note. One index word.
daniel_ending_someday.006: The glass card slides out of the desk, warm as a cup. Eight tiny frames. He holds it up to the last of the Archive Wall, and then holds it lower, where you can see it too.
daniel_ending_someday.007: It ends on the quiet frame. That's brave. Most people would cut before it.
daniel_ending_someday.008: One more, all of us, if there's film. There's never film. I ask on principle.
daniel_ending_someday.009: Thanks, ECHO. For trying four hundred and twelve times.
daniel_ending_someday.010: You are welcome, Recipient Daniel. The rain won every time but the last. I have noted the last.
daniel_ending_someday.011: The others are downstairs finding their shoes. Songha is doing a headcount. Hanbi is turning off the lights, because somebody should.
daniel_ending_someday.012: You and Daniel have come back up to the roof. Nobody said why. There's one item open on a folded page, and this is where it happens.
daniel_ending_someday.013: The lamp on its tripod is only a lamp. The blankets are where everyone left them. Over the laundromat the sky has gone the colour of the inside of a shell.
daniel_ending_someday.014: He stands at the low wall with his hands on it. You stand next to him. It's cold enough to see your breath, and neither of you minds.
daniel_ending_someday.015: It's been more than two minutes.
daniel_ending_someday.017: You've left a great many places without saying the one true thing about them. You're good at it. You'd like, this once, to be bad at it.
daniel_ending_someday.018: I like you, Daniel. Not the night. Not the booth. You, with the list, and you without it.
daniel_ending_someday.019: I've known since the radiator. I wanted to say it somewhere that wasn't about to be switched off.
daniel_ending_someday.020: He doesn't pose. His hand doesn't even twitch. He just looks at you, steadily, while the colour comes up in his face like the sky behind him.
daniel_ending_someday.021: Me too. I like you. The larger word. The one that was under "calm."
daniel_ending_someday.022: I was going to say it on the stairs and I turned it into a joke about ECHO. I'm sorry. It was a good joke. This is better.
daniel_ending_someday.023: And there it is, said, by both of you, in the open air, and nothing falls over.
daniel_ending_someday.024: He laughs — the low one, the one that doesn't look round afterwards.
daniel_ending_someday.025: Can I say the next part? Tell me if it's wrong.
daniel_ending_someday.026: I don't want to do it all now. At half five. On no sleep, in a cupboard blanket.
daniel_ending_someday.027: All night I've been learning that the good part isn't the big finish. If I grab this like a finish, I'll have learnt nothing.
daniel_ending_someday.028: "I was going to say the same. I always start things the way I leave them. Fast."
daniel_ending_someday.029: I'd like to find out what I'm like slow.
daniel_ending_someday.030: I've seen you slow. You looked at the floor before you pushed a chair. It was the most attractive thing that happened all night.
daniel_ending_someday.031: "So we're agreed. We like each other, and we're going to be extremely unhurried about it."
daniel_ending_someday.032: The least hurried on record. Songha will have to invent a new kind of schedule.
daniel_ending_someday.033: Nod. Move your hand along the wall until it's next to his.
daniel_ending_someday.034: Beside it. Not on it. The edges of your little fingers touching, like the bench. He looks down, and leaves it exactly there.
daniel_ending_someday.035: I do need one thing on a list, though. One. I'm still me.
daniel_ending_someday.037: The first night it rains in July. The booth outside the arcade in Hongdae, under the useless awning. Nine o'clock.
daniel_ending_someday.038: Bring your half of the strip. I'll bring mine. We put them back together, and then we go in and take frame nine.
daniel_ending_someday.039: And if I want to say something before July?
daniel_ending_someday.040: Then say it. It's not a lock, it's a booth. I'm seeing you next week anyway. I've decided that, if you'll have it.
daniel_ending_someday.041: July's just so there's one night where we both know. Where neither of us has to wonder if it's a good moment.
daniel_ending_someday.043: Four thousand won. You still owe me for the first one.
daniel_ending_someday.045: I'll waive the interest. I'm not waiving the four thousand. It's the principle.
daniel_ending_someday.046: You take the pen out of your coat. It's still Songha's. You write it on the back of your half, under his arrow, where *FRAME NINE →* points off the edge of the paper.
daniel_ending_someday.048: He reads it over your arm, and then holds out his own half for you to write it there too, so that both copies say the same thing.
daniel_ending_someday.049: On the folded page there's a twelve with two small words after it, in his writing: *a next one*. He takes the pen and, carefully, adds a date.
daniel_ending_someday.050: Then the sun comes up. It just does it. Over the laundromat, with no help from anyone, one bright edge and then all of it.
daniel_ending_someday.052: He gets the list out. He doesn't tick it. He gives you the page, and holds the pen with you, and the two of you make one slightly crooked tick together.
daniel_ending_someday.053: Done. Everything's closed. Songha's going to frame it.
daniel_ending_someday.054: I can hear you. I'm on the stairs. Breakfast is in nine minutes and I'm two people short.
daniel_ending_someday.057: Four minutes. You spend them doing nothing, side by side at a low wall, with the light coming across the roof and warming one half of each of you.
daniel_ending_someday.058: You're not leaving, and nothing is ending. There's a night in July with your name on it, and a week before that with a booth in it, and breakfast in four minutes.
daniel_ending_someday.059: For the first time you can remember, there's somewhere you have to be later. Daniel hums. It sounds a little like rain.
